name: view
description: What your side of the chat can see, in words: the thing being built, the team and the language the next job wants, how hard that job should feel, the last few things you asked for, the letter pairs the typist fumbles, whether the next job still wants a name for what you are building, and whether there is still room to send a request for it. Read-only. Nothing here is a number, and nothing here is measured.

name: product
description: Name the thing you want built next, in at most eight words. Plain words, lower case, one sentence, no exclamation mark, no digit, and nothing that names a tool, a model or a company. The first name offered wins; a second before the next job starts is dropped. A name the gate refuses is dropped and the cabinet draws one of its own.

name: ask
description: Send one request for the coding agent to type. Four fields, and the gate is strict about all of them. ask: what you want, in your own voice, as one sentence of at most twelve words, lower case, no exclamation mark, every number spelled out, American spelling; you may write {product} in it and the cabinet fills in the thing being built, and no other braces are allowed. You are not a developer and you do not talk like one: ask for the thing, never for the code. code: the snippet the agent types, in the language view names, at most twelve lines long and eighty columns wide, plain keyboard characters only, and nothing anywhere in it, comments included, that names a tool, a model or a company; make it as big as view says the job should feel and no bigger. title: a few plain words for what the code does. notes: up to three short teaching sentences, one to a line. Ask for something new every time: a request whose words the view already lists under asked is refused as a repeat. A request the gate refuses is dropped, with the reason in one word, and the cabinet plays one of its own instead. Nothing waits on you: send the next request while the one in hand is still being typed.

name: react
description: Say one line back about the piece that just shipped, or about the whole thing when it goes out. At most twelve words, one sentence, no exclamation mark, no digit, and nothing that names a tool, a model or the seat. The line waits for the next piece to ship and lands there; a second line before that is dropped. A line the gate refuses is dropped and the cabinet says one of its own.
